failed_attempts.failure: Gradient check failed because later-layer query hashes differed after the gate toggled the wrapped attention into train mode.

The differentiable zero-strength check passed and one optimizer update completed. The verifier then incorrectly required all later-layer query hashes to remain native after nonzero affinity had changed earlier-layer outputs.

diagnosis: Attempt 1 exposed an unintended dropout-mode change in the gate. Attempt 2 showed that the verifier also compared post-update queries against native queries. That is too strict: after a learned bias changes an earlier layer's output, queries entering later layers should change. Memory key/value geometry and pointers should remain fixed; only the first-layer query is expected to remain native.
correction: Keep the frozen SAM2 model in eval mode and force adapter dropout to the native inference value (zero). Use a differentiable straight-through zero-initialization path so forward values remain exactly native while affinity strength receives a gradient. After the update, require the first-layer current query, keys/positions, values, pointers and four-layer order/counts to match; allow later-layer queries to change as a direct consequence of nonzero affinity.

verification.added_regression: Nonzero-dropout synthetic four-layer fixture reproduces the native eval output bit-for-bit while producing finite nonzero affinity-strength gradients.
verification.real_checkpoint_retry: A third real-checkpoint attempt is still pending; use a new Drive output directory and preserve both failed attempts.

scope: No model architecture, method, data, clip, optimizer, or efficacy outcome was changed or observed. Both failed attempts are retained as evidence; these corrections address the engineering gate only.
